messages.subject: Re: Challenge
parts:
I don't see the problem in the specific code you've shared, but in general, use string-manipulation to interface between Java and R is an approach that opens you to a world of pain. If your dependent field names contain spaces, or if any of the values in your list of strings contains a comma, then things will go wrong.

You could instead first create a DoubleVector from your dependent field:

double[] dependentValues = new double[data.size()];
for(int row=0;row<data.size();++row) { 
   dependentValues[row] = Double.parseDouble(data.get(row)[dependent_field]);
}
DoubleVector dependentVector = new DoubleArrayVector(dependentValues);

And then you can provide that vector directly to the interpreter using:

engine.put(dependent_field_name, dependentVector);

I don't know what the rest of your code looks like, but be even easier to create an R data.frame from your data:

String[] firstRow = data.get(0);
int numCols = firstRow.length;
int numRows = data.size();
ListVector.NamedBuilder dataframe = ListVector.newNamedBuilder();
dataframe.setAttribute(Symbols.CLASS, new StringArrayVector("data.frame"));
for(int col=0;col<numCols;++col) {
   double values[] = new double[numRows];
   for(int row=0;row<numRows;++row) {
     values[row] = data.get(row)[col];
   }
   dataframe.add(columnNames.get(col), new StringArrayVector(values));
}

engine.put("df", dataframe.build());
engine.put("dependentIndex", dependent_field);

Then you can let the R code take over from there....

HTH,
Alex
